summary: Premise-verified Session 84 merge audit applying the game/product and public-app release lenses. Four new locally executable findings survive live-code review after the Session 83 list reached 4/4: match feedback exposes its admin corpus publicly and accepts replayable browser-supplied game/map claims; outcome and career-style analytics still trust browser-authored win/style facts instead of the certified match envelope; gameplay tuning remains fragmented across runtime, bot, nation artificial intelligence, and user-interface literals beyond the existing convoy/pressure authority; and WinModal blocks its first visible render on optional asynchronous work while delayed callbacks can outlive the modal session. External staging, project-domain delivery, native Obelisk relying-party registration, three-human Alpha, revenue, rollback observation, and founder approval remain unobserved and are not implementation items.

sample.method: live code and contract survey; sample-codebase helper absent; manual survey capped to 20 primary files

nextMoves: Bind feedback and outcome analytics to certified match evidence instead of browser claims.
Finish the executable gameplay-balance authority across runtime, artificial intelligence, and user interface consumers.
Make the post-match experience shell-first, session-scoped, and stale-work-proof.

evidenceBoundary: Local automation cannot manufacture staging, project-domain delivery, relying-party registration, distinct-human Alpha, revenue, rollback observation, or founder approval.
The registry still classifies VaultFront as app while local project truth says game. CANON-018 forbids editing the sibling registry; correction must travel through signed Ark cargo.
No dependency install, paid service, license change, sibling tree edit, or fabricated data is required for the four admitted Session 84 items.
Balance authority work centralizes existing values and verifies equivalence; it does not claim that code review discovered better human-facing tuning.

items.title: Turn certified progression into a replay-safe recoverable fan-out
items.why: MatchProgression inserts gameId into processedGameIds before its first asynchronous leg. A thrown leg leaves the ID claimed and every retry returns duplicate, while PlayerStatsStore can increment Elo and match counters again after restart because match_history has no (persistent_id, game_id) uniqueness. The visible progression stack is individually durable but its orchestration is not recoverable.
items.coreLoopStep: certified match result → rating/achievement/season fan-out → durable receipt
items.recipe: Make PlayerStatsStore atomically idempotent per game across memory and PostgreSQL, add the schema uniqueness invariant, replace pre-claim suppression with explicit in-flight/completed state that releases failed claims, and add concurrency, partial-failure, and fresh-spine replay tests proving each player/game changes rating once while failed fan-out can resume.

L2.recipe: Add store-level player/game idempotency and failure-retry tests.

L3.recipe: Add PostgreSQL advisory serialization plus unique schema protection, concurrent same-process promise coalescing, restart-safe downstream replay, and a canonical completion receipt digest.

executionLog: L3 shipped: PostgreSQL advisory serialization and a player/game unique index backstop restart replay; memory deduplicates the same contract; the progression spine coalesces concurrent calls, releases failed attempts for safe retry, and publishes a stable SHA-256 completion receipt. Focused replay, partial-failure, concurrency, and TypeScript gates passed.

items.title: Make achievement progression an actor-bound profile contract
items.why: GET /api/vaultfront/achievements/:persistentId and the meta-chain variant accept any caller-supplied persistent ID and expose progress without a play token. Newer season and contract reads authenticate the actor and reject cross-player claims. Achievement progress is private player progression and should share that boundary.
items.coreLoopStep: authenticated player → private progression profile → visible Command Center/debrief
items.recipe: Extract an AchievementRouter with injected authentication, bind optional path claims to the verified actor, update the client to send VaultFront identity headers, retain a compatibility path that fails closed on mismatch, add direct router tests, and include the router in the Worker composition budget.

L1.recipe: Require authentication on the two reads.

L2.recipe: Bind the path claim, update the client, and add authorization tests.

L3.recipe: Extract an injected router, test missing/cross-player/valid reads directly, and ratchet Worker composition so the trust boundary cannot drift back.

executionLog: L3 shipped: an injected AchievementRouter requires a verified play actor, rejects cross-player and malformed claims, rate-limits reads, updates client identity headers, and is protected by direct authorization tests plus the Worker composition ratchet (3,098/3,130 lines).

items.title: Make persistence readiness derive from executable store capabilities
items.why: StateScopeLedger declares playtest-pulse as process-only and release-critical even though Worker writes authenticated events through PlaytestEvidenceStore, which uses PostgreSQL when configured and labels process-local fallback honestly. Readiness can therefore emit a false volatility warning from stale handwritten metadata.
items.coreLoopStep: authenticated playtest evidence → durable pulse → honest Alpha/release readiness
items.recipe: Correct the playtest evidence owner/scope, represent store capability separately from effective runtime scope, self-validate declared database-capable owners against an executable capability catalog, and add tests proving ready/absent/failed database postures produce truthful pass/warn/block outcomes.

L1.recipe: Correct the stale playtest-pulse ledger row.

L2.recipe: Test the row against all database postures.

L3.recipe: Add an executable store-capability catalog and a ledger integrity assertion so owner/scope drift fails tests instead of lying in readiness.

executionLog: L3 shipped: PlaytestEvidenceStore is correctly modeled as PostgreSQL-capable with process-local development fallback; capability and effective scope are distinct; contradictory metadata blocks the ledger; disabled/ready/failed database tests and readiness/passport integration are green.

items.axis: feature depth / game loop / speed / testability
items.title: Extract the Vault Pressure climax into a deterministic domain kernel
items.why: VaultFrontExecution is roughly 2,900 lines and directly owns the three-delivery breach threshold, 90-second expiry, win trigger, and fallback-to-two behavior inside mutable maps. That flagship climax has no pure transition contract or file-size ratchet, making balance-preserving changes harder to prove than the newer reward planner.
items.coreLoopStep: convoy deliveries → pressure escalation → breach window → extraction win or recoverable expiry
items.recipe: Extract a pure VaultPressureKernel that receives prior state plus certified transition input and emits next state/events, preserve the current three-delivery and expiry semantics exactly, adapt VaultFrontExecution as composition only, add exhaustive transition/property tests, and add a source composition ratchet that forbids the extracted state-machine body from returning.

L1.recipe: Extract pressure arithmetic into pure helpers.

L2.recipe: Model delivery/expiry transitions and cover threshold edge cases.

L3.recipe: Emit typed domain events, exhaustively verify deterministic transition sequences, integrate without balance changes, and ratchet the composition boundary.

executionLog: L3 shipped: the three-delivery breach climax is a pure typed transition kernel with open, expiry, final-tick, normalization, victory, and deterministic sequence coverage. VaultFrontExecution composes the kernel without balance changes and is ratcheted at the exact formatter-stable 2,917-line baseline.

items.title: Turn match ratings into certified, replay-safe feedback evidence
items.why: GET /api/admin/match-ratings returns the full rating/comment corpus without an admin check. POST /api/vaultfront/match-rating authenticates an actor but trusts browser-supplied gameId and mapName, allows unlimited duplicate ratings, and stores only process-local arrays. A caller can pollute map feedback and a public reader can retrieve it.
items.coreLoopStep: certified participant → one private match rating → operator-only aggregate → product learning
items.recipe: Extract a MatchFeedbackRouter and store; authenticate the actor, load the certified archived match to prove participation and derive map identity, enforce one actor/game rating with explicit conflict semantics, persist in PostgreSQL with an honestly labeled process-local development fallback, protect the aggregate with the configured admin contract, and cover missing/cross-game/replay/admin/durability paths directly.

L1.recipe: Add admin authorization and duplicate suppression.

L2.recipe: Extract the route, bind actor participation to certified match evidence, and derive map identity server-side.

L3.recipe: Add transactionally unique PostgreSQL storage, honest fallback scope, aggregate receipts, direct authorization/idempotency tests, and a composition ratchet preventing inline route regression.

executionLog: S84: Added certificate-bound actor feedback route/store, server-authoritative map attribution, persistent idempotency, aggregate-only admin reporting, route-policy coverage, schema migration, and focused regression tests. Verified Vitest 28/28, tsc, worker composition, and route-policy coverage exit 0.

items.title: Make outcome and career style one certified match projection
items.why: ExperimentRouter records won, behind-at-minute-eight, duration, and engagement from a browser POST; Worker also accepts browser-authored style-history mutations and exposes arbitrary player style reads. The certified match envelope already contains authoritative result and VaultFront metrics, but these analytics bypass it.
items.coreLoopStep: certified result → outcome/style projection → private career profile + honest aggregate
items.recipe: Move outcome and play-style derivation into pure shared kernels fed by AuthoritativeMatchOutcome, add the missing certified metrics to the envelope, fan the projection out inside MatchProgression with player/game idempotency and explicit storage scope, retire browser-authored result/style mutations with 410 tombstones, split client interaction observations from certified outcome facts, actor-bind career reads, and include verifiable projection receipts in progression evidence.

L1.recipe: Retire browser-authored win/style facts and actor-bind reads.

L2.recipe: Derive outcome/style from the certified envelope and add replay-safe process-local projections.

L3.recipe: Create pure shared kernels, durable player/game history, certified-vs-observed summary separation, digest-bound receipts, direct route/spine tests, and client migration with no duplicate authority.

executionLog: S84: Replaced browser-authored outcome/style facts with a certified match projection. Added shared pure style classification, signed-result metric fan-out, PostgreSQL/process-local idempotent outcome storage, actor-bound career history, admin-only certified aggregates, authenticated deduplicated interaction observations, schema/readiness ownership, and regression coverage. Verified 56/56 focused tests, TypeScript, worker composition, and route-policy coverage exit 0.

items.axis: feature depth / artificial intelligence / speed / release truth
items.title: Complete the executable gameplay-balance authority
items.why: config/vaultfront-balance.v1.json owns convoy rewards and pressure, but VaultFrontExecution still embeds dozens of capture, defense, command, comeback, event, intelligence, and economic values. Jam Breaker cost is separately duplicated in VaultFrontExecution, BotExecution, NationExecution, tests, and ControlPanel. Runtime, artificial intelligence, UI, and release evidence can silently disagree.
items.coreLoopStep: versioned tuning → simulation + bots + nation AI + HUD → deterministic release envelope
items.recipe: Extend the versioned balance schema across every remaining VaultFront gameplay subsystem without changing values; expose frozen typed projections; make runtime, BotExecution, NationExecution, and UI fallbacks consume them; add a structural no-embedded-tunables ratchet and cross-consumer parity tests; expand deterministic balance verification and release lineage so any tuning change produces one reviewable fingerprint.

L1.recipe: Centralize Jam Breaker cost/cooldown across runtime, bots, and UI.

L2.recipe: Move defense, comeback, and command parameters into typed config with parity tests.

L3.recipe: Migrate all remaining gameplay tunables, validate the schema and invariants, ban duplicated literals structurally, extend the deterministic envelope, and bind one authority fingerprint through release evidence.

executionLog: S84: Promoted 15 gameplay domains (simulation, vault, defense, comeback, economy, events, AI, placement, reward dynamics, mutators, and related systems) into one validated versioned authority without changing live values. Added number-to-bigint runtime projection, mutator projection, Bot/Nation/UI parity, a public SHA-256 authority fingerprint, release lineage binding, structural duplication checker, deterministic envelope, and exact 2,907-line execution ratchet. Verified 28,125 scenarios with zero counterexamples, 53/53 focused tests, TypeScript, and all contract gates exit 0.

items.title: Make the post-match experience shell-first and session-scoped
items.why: WinModal.show awaits pattern loading and recap assignment before setting isVisible. Optional network latency can leave the decisive post-match moment blank. Multiple unmanaged timeouts, animation frames, and promise callbacks continue after hide/reopen, while Elo animation uses one browser-global lastElo value despite an actor-bound certified history already being returned.
items.coreLoopStep: match end → immediate recap shell → progressive certified enrichment → safe requeue/exit
items.recipe: Introduce a post-match session orchestrator with a generation token, timer/animation registry, optional-task deadlines, and stale-result rejection; render the recap shell immediately; hydrate independent panels in parallel without blocking actions; cancel every delayed effect on hide/reopen; derive previous Elo from the authenticated history rather than global browser state; and add fake-timer/deferred-promise tests proving immediate visibility, cancellation, one telemetry flush, and account-safe rating animation.

L1.recipe: Set visibility before optional awaits and clear tracked timeouts.

L2.recipe: Add generation-based stale-result rejection, parallel hydration, and actor-safe Elo history.

L3.recipe: Extract a reusable lifecycle orchestrator covering timers, animation frames, deadlines, telemetry flush, progressive hydration, and exhaustive hide/reopen race tests while tightening the WinModal composition ratchet.

executionLog: S84: Extracted a generation-scoped post-match lifecycle owner for every timer, animation frame, deadline, and cancellable promise. The decisive shell now renders synchronously; certified contracts are fetched once and shared by seasonal and actor-bound Elo views; independent panels hydrate concurrently; hide/reopen and in-flight rematch/share results cannot commit stale state; browser-global Elo history was retired; and the shared certified play-style classifier now drives the UI. Verified 17/17 focused lifecycle/composition tests, TypeScript, and the full contract suite exit 0.
